requirements.statement: The main import reason page's h1 reads 'Main import reason' and its browser title 'Main import reason - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
requirements.why: The prototype names the page 'Main import reason' and wins by default on a page name; no DR1 judgement or real constraint covers the heading.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the h1 and title read 'Main reason for import' (repo-frontend-p7-003, trace-animals-fit-p7-003); the fit spec and the tests repo's import-reason spec assert that wording (repo-tests-p1-067) and must change with it, as must the machine-draft Welsh title.

requirements.statement: The main import reason page shows the caption 'About the consignment' above its h1, and the question 'What is the main reason for importing the animals?' is the reason radio group's visually hidden legend rather than a heading.
requirements.why: The target design and the real service already agree: the page heading stands as the question, and screen-reader users hear the legend as the group's name.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p7-004 and trace-animals-fit-p7-006 show the caption and the hidden legend today.

requirements.statement: Both pages sit in the journey layout: a Back link, a strip with a 'Draft' status tag and the notification reference above the caption, and on error a 'There is a problem' error summary between that strip and the caption.
requirements.why: The target design renders both pages this way and the real service already does; the shell area owns the layout itself.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p7-010-m1 and trace-animals-fit-p12-061 show the Draft strip; trace-animals-fit-p7-059 shows the error summary above the caption.

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set the main import reason is one radio choice of five reasons, in this order: Internal market; Transhipment or onward travel; Transit; Re-entry; Temporary admission horses. The answer belongs to the notification as a whole, only one reason is held, no reason is pre-selected on a notification without one, and the list is the same for every live-animal commodity. The germinal-products set's own copy of the page carries its own two-reason list of Internal market and Transit.
requirements.why: The policy page, the target design and the real service all offer the same five reasons in the same order, as a single-select answer at notification level, and the policy page names which of them the germinals journey offers. The 9 October ruling puts germinal products in a sibling set with its own catalogue, so the reduced list belongs to that set's copy of the page.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-007 and trace-animals-fit-p7-013 show the five reasons in this order today. The policy page marks the reason field block 'At least one' while the field itself is a single-select enumeration and no field records a second reason (confluence-6497338582-p3-006): the single-select reading is what both the prototype and the real service build, so one reason is held.

requirements.statement: Each reason carries its hint: Internal market 'For imports of animals intended for sale or use in Great Britain (England, Scotland or Wales).'; Transhipment or onward travel 'For animals intended for direct travel to a third country, that will stay only within the same port or airport in Great Britain while moving to another means of transport.'; Transit 'For animals moving through Great Britain for direct travel to a third country, that will enter Great Britain at one port or airport and leave from a different one within England, Scotland or Wales.'; Re-entry 'For animals authorised for re-entry, or rejected exports re-entering Great Britain.'; Temporary admission horses 'For horses authorised for temporary entry.'
requirements.why: The five hints are word for word the same in the target design and the real service.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-008 to repo-frontend-p7-012 hold the same five hints today.

requirements.statement: A main import reason is optional to proceed: Save and continue with no reason chosen shows no error and moves on.
requirements.why: The policy page makes the reason mandatory to submit but lets the trader move past the page without it, the target design makes it optional to proceed, and the real service already does.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-013 and trace-e2e-p5-062-m1 show a blank reason accepted today; no fit or tests-repo page test pins it (repo-tests-p1-074, trace-animals-fit-p7-076).

requirements.statement: Each reason that needs follow-up questions opens them in a standard GOV.UK conditional reveal directly under its own radio, so the reason and its follow-ups are answered in one submit; Re-entry has no reveal and saves on its own; every reveal is hidden until its reason is chosen. Without JavaScript every reveal shows open and the page still works, because only the chosen reason's follow-ups are validated and saved.
requirements.why: The target design asks the follow-ups as reveals on the reason page; the real service moved them there in DR1 parity (inc-067), so it already matches. The policy page names no extra field for Re-entry. The 9 October afternoon ruling requires every page to work fully without JavaScript, which GOV.UK's conditional reveal already gives.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-015 and trace-animals-fit-p7-019 show the four reveals under their radios today, and trace-e2e-p4-104 shows Re-entry saving alone.

requirements.statement: Choosing Internal market reveals the radio question 'Purpose in the internal market' (medium legend) with eleven options, in this order: Transfer of ownership - Sale/gift; Transfer of ownership - Rescue; Breeding; Research; Racing, competition, show or training; Approved premises or body; Companion animal not for resale or rehoming; Production; Slaughter; Fattening; Restocking. The answer belongs to the notification as a whole, no purpose is pre-selected when the reveal first opens, and in the live-animals set all eleven are offered for every commodity. The germinal-products set's own copy of the reveal offers four: Transfer of ownership - Sale/gift, Breeding, Research and Production.
requirements.why: The policy page, the target design and the real service ask the same purpose question with the same eleven options in the same order for live animals, as a single-select answer at notification level, and the policy page names which four the germinals journey offers.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-017, repo-frontend-p7-018 and trace-animals-fit-p7-023 show the legend and the eleven purposes in this order today.

requirements.statement: Each of the eleven internal market purposes carries its own hint beneath its label: Transfer of ownership - Sale/gift describes any movement aimed at sale or transfer of ownership, including gifts; Transfer of ownership - Rescue rehoming, adoption or fostering; Breeding reproduction and breeding programmes; Research 'Animals for use in scientific or medical research.'; Racing, competition, show or training 'Animals to participate in competitive or training events.'; Approved premises or body 'Animals for exhibition, zoos, collections, or conservation programmes where a licence or approval is needed.'; Companion animal not for resale or rehoming privately owned animals that cannot meet the non-commercial rules; Production 'Animals that are farmed for the production of meat, milk, eggs, wool or any other animal product or by-product.'; Slaughter 'Animals to be slaughtered and processed for meat production shortly after arrival into Great Britain.'; Fattening 'Animals to be fattened for meat production.'; Restocking 'To replenish or enhance populations of species, for example, restocking of game or fish.'
requirements.why: The eleven purpose hints are word for word the same in the target design and the real service.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-019 to repo-frontend-p7-029 hold the same eleven hints today.

requirements.statement: With Internal market chosen and no purpose, Save and continue is refused: 'Select a purpose in the internal market' shows in the error summary (linking to the purpose radios) and inline on the purpose question, which alone takes the error style; Internal market stays checked with its reveal open.
requirements.why: The policy page makes the internal market purpose mandatory to proceed, the target design requires a chosen reason's follow-ups, and the real service already enforces the purpose with this message. The policy page gives no error wording for this section (confluence-6497338582-p3-068), so the service's own messages stand.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-030 and trace-animals-fit-p7-065 show the message and its placement today.

requirements.statement: Internal market with a purpose (for example Breeding) saves in one submit, and on return both are offered back: Internal market checked, its reveal open and the purpose checked.
requirements.why: The target design and the real service both save the reason and purpose together.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-064 and trace-e2e-p4-113 show the save and the answers offered back today.

requirements.statement: Choosing Transhipment or onward travel reveals one question only, a 'Destination country' select with no hint; it does not ask for a port of exit.
requirements.why: The policy page asks for a destination country on Transhipment or onward travel and on Transit, and for no other reason, and the target design and the real service both ask transhipment for the destination country alone. The policy page's condition reads 'Transit or Transhipment or onward travel', which could be read as three alternatives (confluence-6497338582-p3-041); the two-permitted-value reading is the one the target design and the real service both build.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-031 and trace-animals-fit-p7-035 show the single destination country select today.

requirements.statement: Choosing Transit reveals two selects in this order: 'Port of exit' then 'Destination country', both without a hint.
requirements.why: The policy page asks Transit for both a port of exit and a destination country, and the target design and the real service ask transit for the same two questions in the same order.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-032 and trace-animals-fit-p7-036 show port of exit then destination country today.

requirements.statement: Choosing Temporary admission horses reveals two questions in this order: 'Exit date' then a 'Port of exit' select with no hint.
requirements.why: The policy page asks Temporary admission horses for an exit date and a port of exit, and the target design and the real service ask the same two questions in the same order.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-033 and trace-animals-fit-p7-037 show exit date then port of exit today.

requirements.statement: Every 'Destination country' select on the reason page starts with an empty option reading 'Select one', selected when nothing is chosen, followed straight by the countries with no divider line. It is a plain GOV.UK select the trader picks from rather than types into; where the accessible autocomplete has already replaced it, 'Select one' shows as far as that component allows.
requirements.why: The target design's placeholder is 'Select one' with no divider, and it wins by default on this copy with nothing to override it. The policy page has the trader choose the destination from a list rather than typing it. The 9 October afternoon ruling keeps the import reason's exit fields as plain selects and has a row's copy follow the prototype as far as an already-added autocomplete can show it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the select opens on 'Select a country' followed by a disabled divider line (repo-frontend-p7-035, trace-animals-fit-p7-043, trace-e2e-p4-106).

requirements.statement: The destination country selects for transhipment and transit both read from the one shared country list the service uses for country of origin, server-rendered as plain selects with no browser-side lookup.
requirements.why: The target design reuses its country-of-origin list for the destination and the real service already reuses its origin list; the policy page does not name a separate destination list. The 9 October afternoon ruling keeps these fields as plain selects and leaves rolling the accessible autocomplete out to more screens to EUDPA-635 and a follow-on ticket recorded in deferred.md, so the transhipment destination country does not get it here.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-035 shows the destination list built from countries.originCountries() today.

requirements.statement: The transhipment and transit 'Destination country' selects offer reference-data's GBNAG_SPS_EX countries plus their subdivisions, each subdivision labelled '<territory> (<parent>)', all sorted alphabetically as the origin page sorts them. The content is what reference-data serves: trade-imports-stub locally and in CDP dev, real MDM in CDP test. No entry is added, removed or respelt in code.
requirements.why: The target design offers EU outermost regions and territories beside the countries, labelled with their parent, and the policy page has the destination country list come from MDM. The 9 October ruling lifts DR1's MDM block, because no reference list waits on MDM: the list is built now against reference-data as it is. It also rules that list content is MDM's to own, not the prototype's.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the select lists 31 countries, the 27 EU states plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland, with no subdivisions (trace-animals-fit-p7-044, trace-e2e-p4-106). It builds after the reference-lists theme's stub tidy-up row, which changes the names and counts its tests assert (ruling claim 149).

requirements.statement: Every 'Port of exit' select on the reason page starts with an empty option reading 'Select one', selected when nothing is chosen, followed straight by the ports with no divider line. It is a plain GOV.UK select; where the accessible autocomplete has already replaced it, 'Select one' shows as far as that component allows.
requirements.why: The target design's placeholder is 'Select one' with no divider, and it wins by default on this copy with nothing to override it. The 9 October afternoon ruling keeps the import reason's exit fields as plain selects, has how a list reads follow the prototype, and has a row's copy follow the prototype as far as an already-added autocomplete can show it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the select opens on 'Select port of exit' followed by a disabled divider line (repo-frontend-p7-037, trace-animals-fit-p7-045).

requirements.statement: The transit and temporary admission 'Port of exit' selects both offer the whole ports-of-entry list from trade-imports-reference-data, the same list the port of entry question uses. Entries appear as MDM serves them, duplicates and misspellings included: these go to the MDM team as a data report, are not corrected in code, and no test pins them.
requirements.why: The policy page has the trader choose the port of exit from the port of entry list, because exit and entry share the same list of ports, and has that list come from MDM. The target design gives exit its own list of animal-approved border control posts; the 9 October ruling replaces that for now, because MDM carries no approved-for-animals flag. It also rules that the duplicate and misspelt ports are MDM's real data.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-037, trace-animals-fit-p7-045 and trace-e2e-p4-108 show both selects offering the 78-entry ports-of-entry list today. Its labels and order change under their own requirements, and any test that pins a misspelt or duplicated name stops doing so (ruling claim 171).

requirements.statement: The exit date is one text field using the MOJ date picker, labelled 'Exit date' with a 'Choose date' calendar (Monday-first weeks, picking a day fills the field as day/month/year); surrounding spaces are trimmed before the date is read, and no earliest or latest date is set.
requirements.why: The target design and the real service use the same picker, label and calendar, and the policy page sets no bound on the exit date beyond its format. The MoJ date picker is one of the components the 9 October afternoon ruling accepts, and its design question 12 covers only the germinal dates read from a document, so the exit date keeps its calendar.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-038, repo-frontend-p7-052 and trace-animals-fit-p7-038 to trace-animals-fit-p7-041 show the same picker, label and calendar today. The hint wording and the typed form the field accepts are settled separately.

requirements.statement: With Transhipment or onward travel chosen and no listed destination country, Save and continue is refused with 'Select a destination country' in the error summary and inline on the select, which takes the GOV.UK select error style.
requirements.why: The policy page makes the destination country mandatory to proceed once its condition is met, the target design requires it, and the real service already refuses with this message.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-039 and repo-frontend-p7-039-m1 hold the rule and message today; no fit or E2E trace submits transhipment without a country (trace-animals-fit-p7-077), so a test should pin it.

requirements.statement: With Transit chosen, a missing port of exit shows 'Select a port of exit' and a missing destination country 'Select a destination country', both together when both are missing, port first, each in the summary and inline; the reveal stays open and an answered field is kept.
requirements.why: The policy page makes both transit follow-ups mandatory to proceed, the target design requires them in this order, and the real service already does.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p7-062 to trace-animals-fit-p7-064 show both messages, their order and the kept port today.

requirements.statement: With Temporary admission horses chosen, a blank exit date shows 'Enter an exit date' and a missing port 'Select a port of exit', both together when both are missing, date first, each in the summary and inline; the reveal stays open and an answered field is kept.
requirements.why: The policy page makes the exit date and port of exit mandatory to proceed once their condition is met, the target design requires both in this order, and the real service already does.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p7-067 to trace-animals-fit-p7-069 show both messages and their order today.

requirements.statement: An exit date that is not a real calendar date (for example 31/2/2026) is refused with 'Enter a real date', in the summary and inline, with the typed value kept in the field; a past or future date is not refused.
requirements.why: The target design checks only that the exit date is present and real, the policy page sets no bound beyond the format, and the real service applies the same two rules.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-042 holds the 'Enter a real date' rule today, but no fit test proves it (repo-frontend-p7-115), so a test should pin it and confirm the typed value is redisplayed.

requirements.statement: When the reason page is shown again after a refused submit, the chosen reason stays selected with its reveal open, the other reveals stay hidden, and the user's entries are shown again.
requirements.why: The target design and the real service both re-render the page with the user's answers in place, and the 26 October ruling holds that what a trader typed is never dropped.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-053 shows the reason, its open reveal and the user's entries kept on re-render today.

requirements.statement: Only the chosen reason's follow-ups are validated and saved; changing the reason removes the earlier reason's answers that the new one does not ask, so returning to Internal market after switching away offers no purpose and asks for it again.
requirements.why: The target design clears follow-up answers that belong to reasons no longer chosen, and the real service already purges them on save.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-047, repo-frontend-p7-048 and trace-e2e-p4-114 show the purge today.

requirements.statement: The notification holds one destination country and one port of exit answer, each reached through its own form field per reveal, and every reveal that asks for it is prefilled from the saved answer, so a Transit country is still offered under Transhipment.
requirements.why: The target design names a separate field per reveal, but DR1 judged that the per-branch names are a DOM artefact, not extra questions, and that carrying a shared answer between reveals is not a requirement (inc-067); that judgement on the same difference stands. The policy page holds both answers at notification level.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-050 and trace-e2e-p4-117 show one stored country and port prefilled in every reveal today.

requirements.statement: The reason, internal market purpose, certification purpose and unweaned answers are stored as the service's codes (for example internalMarket, breeding, further-keeping, yes), not as their displayed labels.
requirements.why: Stored values are a persistence contract with the backend and other services that the prototype, which stores labels, cannot express; the ruling lets that constraint override the prototype.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-007 and trace-animals-fit-p12-007 show the coded values stored today.

requirements.statement: A submitted reason, certification purpose or unweaned value that is not one of the offered options is refused with 'Select a valid option', linking to and focusing the group's first radio, with no option left checked and the other question's valid answer kept; a refused submit writes nothing to the notification.
requirements.why: Server-side validation that refuses tampered values and never saves a refused submit is a real constraint the prototype cannot express (it silently drops or stores them), so it overrides the prototype.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-014, repo-frontend-p7-091 and trace-e2e-p4-115-m1 show the refusal and that nothing is written today.

requirements.statement: When either page is refused on submit, the browser title is prefixed 'Error: ' and the page is answered with HTTP 400; each inline message carries a visually hidden 'Error:' prefix.
requirements.why: The 'Error: ' title prefix is how GOV.UK tells screen-reader users a validation error has happened; the prototype's title omits it, but accessible validation is a real constraint the prototype does not express.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p7-059 and trace-animals-fit-p12-029 show the 'Error: ' prefix and HTTP 400 today.

requirements.statement: When a saved destination country, port of exit or certification purpose is no longer in the reference list, reopening the page says so ('The saved destination country is no longer available. Select a country from the list.', 'The saved port of exit is no longer available. Select a port from the list.', 'The certification purpose you chose is no longer offered. Select a purpose from the list.') and blanks it in every reveal.
requirements.why: A saved answer going stale against reference data is a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express, so the real service keeps handling it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-043, repo-frontend-p7-044 and repo-frontend-p7-092 hold these messages today; no fit test proves them (repo-frontend-p7-114).

requirements.statement: If saving either page fails, the page is shown again with the user's entries and the shared recoverable-error message, with HTTP 500.
requirements.why: A failed save is a persistence condition the prototype cannot express; the real service already recovers from it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-056 and repo-frontend-p7-102 show the recoverable error today.

requirements.statement: The main import reason page's Back link goes to the previous journey page, What are you importing, and to the notification hub when the page was opened from the hub.
requirements.why: The target design links Back to the previous page in the linear journey; it wins by default and no DR1 judgement covers this Back link.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the Back link always goes to the notification hub (repo-frontend-p7-002, trace-animals-fit-p7-008), and a fit test pins it (repo-frontend-p7-065).

requirements.statement: Save and continue on the main import reason page goes next to Commodity details in the linear journey, and back to the notification hub when the page was opened from the hub.
requirements.why: The target design follows the reason with Commodity details; it wins by default and nothing overrides the journey order here.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the opening run goes from the reason page to Additional details (trace-e2e-p5-061, repo-tests-p1-075), and outside the run to the hub (trace-animals-fit-p7-053).

requirements.statement: Both pages end with a 'Save and continue' button, a secondary 'Save and return to overview' button and a 'Cancel and return to overview' link to the notification hub.
requirements.why: The target design gives both pages the three journey controls, and the real service already has them.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p7-050 to trace-animals-fit-p7-052 and trace-animals-fit-p12-017 to trace-animals-fit-p12-019 show all three controls today.

requirements.statement: 'Save and return to overview' on the main import reason page makes exactly the same checks as 'Save and continue', and differs only in where it goes when every answer passes: the notification hub rather than the next journey page. A missing or invalid follow-up answer keeps the trader on the page with an error for each one, the chosen reason still checked, its reveal open and the entries shown again. When amending, the 'Save and return' (review) action makes the same checks and goes to the review page; while a template is being edited from its review it saves the template and returns to that review.
requirements.why: The 26 October ruling, which outranks every other source, makes Save and return to overview run exactly the checks Save and continue runs, with an error for each missing or invalid answer and the trader kept on the page, and says no page is an exception; it replaces the earlier soft save recorded in c-211 and its plants counterpart c-313. The germinal-products set's copy of this page is a sibling set in the same frontend with the same two buttons, so it takes the same rule even though the ruling names only live animals and high-risk plants (ruling claim 24).
requirements.deltaNote: The 26 October ruling records that today this button skips the checks Save and continue makes on this very page (ruling-sam-2026-10-26-p1-001); no fit or E2E trace in this area shows the button's behaviour (trace-animals-fit-p7-079), so the builder reads the shared save actions and changes only what differs.

requirements.statement: When the main import reason page is opened while editing a template from its review, the Back link goes to that template's review, and saving saves the template and returns to its review with a '<title> has been updated' message. Template mode walks this same page, never a copy of it, so later changes to the page carry into template mode; it applies to the animals sets only.
requirements.why: The target design lets a template be edited page by page from its review; the templates ruling makes template mode another way through the same journey pages, with Back links that follow the context the page was opened in, and builds it on the pages as they stand. The templates area owns the template itself.
requirements.deltaNote: No today source in this area shows template editing reaching this page.

requirements.statement: The main import reason task counts as complete once a reason allowed for the notification is saved with valid follow-ups (Internal market an allowed purpose; Transhipment a listed country; Transit a listed port and country; Temporary admission horses a real exit date and listed port; Re-entry nothing more), whether or not Additional details is answered; with no reason saved it is not complete.
requirements.why: The target design judges the reason section on its own answers and has Additional details as a separate task.
requirements.deltaNote: On latest main the 'Main reason for import' row completes only once the Additional details page after it is saved too (trace-e2e-p4-112, trace-e2e-p4-116); the fit traces at an older commit showed it complete on the reason alone (trace-animals-fit-p7-054).

requirements.statement: The additional details page is headed 'Additional details' (title 'Additional details - Import notification service - GOV.UK') with the caption 'Commodity details'.
requirements.why: The target design and the real service already agree on the heading, title and caption.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p12-001 and trace-animals-fit-p12-002 show the same title, heading and caption today. The page stays at /additional-details, not the prototype's /additional-animal-details path, because no increment changes a real URL path to match the prototype (ruling claim 72).

requirements.statement: The additional details page asks 'What are the animals certified for?' (medium legend) as radios with sixteen options and no hints, in this order: Further keeping; Slaughter; Confined establishment; Germinal products; Registered equine animal; Travelling circus/animal act; Exhibition; Event or activity near borders; Release into the wild; Dispatch centre; Relaying area / purification centre; Ornamental aquaculture establishment; Technical use; Quarantine or similar establishment; Live aquatic animals for human consumption; Other. The answer belongs to the notification as a whole, the same sixteen are offered whatever the commodity, and Other reveals nothing.
requirements.why: The policy page, the target design and the real service list the same sixteen values in the same order as a single-select answer the trader gives at notification level; reference-data serves no certification purposes list, so the frontend's own list stays the source.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-088 and trace-animals-fit-p12-006 show the sixteen options in this order today; trace-animals-fit-p12-009 shows them unfiltered by species.

requirements.deltaNote: Today the hint reads 'This information can be found on the ITAHC.' (repo-frontend-p7-087, trace-animals-fit-p12-005, trace-e2e-p5-065); the machine-draft Welsh hint changes with it.

requirements.statement: When it applies, the additional details page asks 'Does the consignment contain any unweaned animals?' (medium legend) with the hint 'These are animals that are still feeding from their mother.' and the options Yes and No, after the certification question and once per notification; Yes leads to no further question.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-093 and trace-animals-fit-p12-011 to trace-animals-fit-p12-013 show the same question today.

requirements.why: The policy page names the commodities the unweaned rule covers, and it outranks the prototype on which commodity codes a conditional rule applies to; equines and cattle are the two of them today's live-animal catalogue holds, and the 9 October afternoon ruling has the commodity questions go ahead on today's commodity data.

requirements.why: The policy page makes both answers mandatory to submit rather than mandatory to proceed, the target design does not validate the page, and the real service already lets it be saved blank and drops an unweaned answer the commodities no longer call for.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-090, repo-frontend-p7-097 and repo-frontend-p7-098 show both answers optional and the unweaned answer kept only while it applies today; no page test submits it blank (repo-tests-p1-083, trace-animals-fit-p12-063).

requirements.statement: The additional details task counts as complete when the page does not apply, or when each question it asks has an answer from its options; a cattle consignment with only one answer is not complete.
requirements.why: The target design judges the section by the questions the page asks, and the real service already completes it once those are answered.
